meta.note: A thin Monday. The two-day window overlaps with the weekend editions: identi, Harbour Brewing, Skydance, the mountain logos, thatgamecompany and the agents-as-feed essay already ran on 3 and 4 October and are not repeated. The rest was deals, collectibles, AI politics and data-centre news. One UX Collective essay was member-only and could not be read beyond the opening. No feed failures, the State of Brand sitemap returned no page in the window, three paid Substack posts were removed upfront.

stories.title: AI is removing the repetitions that used to make designers senior
stories.blurb: Krutchinsky reads five signals, from an HPE job ad declaring the end of the pixel-pushing specialist to postings that make failure states and fallback paths a hiring requirement. Her point: companies raise the bar for judgment while cutting the routine work people learned it from. Each signal comes with a concrete exercise, such as marking which sentences in a case study only prove you produced something hard.

sources.name: Marina Krutchinsky
sources.headline: Before Monday: HPE, Lenovo, UserTesting point to an uncomfortable shift in how design expertise gets built and valued

stories.title: DRZZL drops dark glass for a squeeze bottle and neon type
stories.blurb: Derek&Eric branded an influencer's olive oil against a category of muted greens and Mediterranean nostalgia: stacked custom lettering by Studio Drama, orange and yellow on dark green, a plastic squeeze bottle. Design Week reads it as part of a wider shift in food branding toward utility and high-contrast visuals built for phone screens. A short news piece, the images carry most of it.

sources.name: Design Week
